survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is based on published Education at a Glance 2025 indicators rather than an author-run student-level microdata analysis. As such, the note does not report the underlying complex survey design variables (e.g., student sampling weights or replicate weights) or any analyst-applied weighting procedure. The figures and indicators are presented for the latest available reference year and are linked to OECD indicator tables and methodological notes, which are where the original sampling/weighting and estimation procedures are documented. For users wishing to reproduce or extend the indicators, the appropriate weighting and variance estimation approach should be taken from the Education at a Glance 2025 “Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes” and the OECD Handbook for Internationally Comparative Education Statistics 2018.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive country note summarising system-level indicators (e.g., attainment, unemployment by education level, expenditure per student, teacher turnover) rather than modelling cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. Because it does not conduct an original student-level ILSA/PV-based analysis, plausible values handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is not reported here because the note relies on OECD’s already-produced indicator estimates; the detailed imputation/handling rules are expected to be documented in the linked OECD methodological sources rather than in this short narrative.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used OECD Education at a Glance 2025 indicator data for Greece for the latest available reference year(s) as specified in the corresponding OECD tables (e.g., Table A3.5, B4.3, C1.1, C1.2, D8.4). No additional student-level inclusion/exclusion criteria are described in this country note.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Greece provides a descriptive overview of education-system characteristics, with emphasis on tertiary education. It reports indicator trends and cross-sectional comparisons using OECD’s compiled data sources and published estimation procedures, including unemployment rates by educational attainment, attainment shares among young adults, participation and progression into tertiary education, field-of-study distributions, international student mobility, and education expenditure by level and funding source. The note also summarises teacher workforce dynamics (turnover), teacher salary comparisons, compulsory instruction time, school holidays, and instructional time allocation to core subjects. Because it is not an original student-level large-scale assessment analysis, it does not specify plausible values, missing-data handling, or ML model performance; instead, it points readers to the Education at a Glance 2025 indicator tables and the “Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes” for the underlying measurement and estimation details.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction corresponds to a descriptive OECD country note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment study with an analytic sample, model estimation, or reported ML outcomes. Consequently, fields such as total_students, per-country sample sizes, plausible values handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not applicable or not reported within the note itself. The note’s substantive content is indicator-based and is intended to be interpreted alongside the linked OECD tables and methodological documentation.
